answer: Because the shale audit recomputes usage from the nadir history, a padded declaration is a losing trade rather than a trivial one. A farm running 74 keys as a result pays for 74 separate budgets, and each of them has to be real to survive a spot-check of the pigment declaration. Each identity declares a compute budget of 113 units per epoch and the declaration is bound to its signing key, so two identities cannot share one budget without a visible collision. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
